$comment: GOLDEN FIXTURE — the operation-facade envelope this adapter consumes.
Issue #5052 (U17a), EPIC #4910. R14, ADP half, acceptance 2 (logic half).
READ THE PROVENANCE NOTE FIRST: ../../contracts/PROVISIONING-CONTRACT.md.
It states exactly which fields below are derived from something B published
and which are UNRESOLVED. This file is not a claim about B's contract.
Why the split matters: the story requires fixtures derived from B's published
contract shape or a captured real response, never from the adapter's own
expected shape — because an adapter and a fixture built from the same
assumption agree with each other about a contract B never publishes, and the
agreement reads as verification.
B has published: the three-field substrate (`name`, `version`, `owner`) that
is on every harness contract, and the routing rule that long-running work
which outlives a single call is a `job`. B has NOT published an operation
facade: `modules/harness/jobs/` does not exist and `job.schema.json` is not
written. So the envelope here is B's; the operation-specific payload fields
are marked unresolved rather than invented, and the adapter does not depend
on them.
`test_provisioning_adapter.py` executes this file, per the executed-contract
convention of contracts/hitl-ticket/v1/. A fixture nothing executes prevents
nothing.

substrate.$comment: Derived from modules/harness/contracts/README.md: 'Three fields are present on *every* contract: name, version, owner. That's the minimum substrate the harness needs to register, dedupe, and route questions.' The README marks the JSON-Schema envelope aspirational and this substrate not.
substrate.name: job

$comment: From the README's decision tree, quoted: 'Long-running work that outlives a
single call? -> job.schema.json'. Workspace provisioning is exactly that,
which is why U17a initiates through an operation facade rather than calling
a synchronous tool verb. This entry records the routing decision and the
published sentence it follows from — it is not a field of any contract.
why_a_job_and_not_a_tool.published_state: target — README table row only, no schema file, no implementation directory

$comment: Fields the ADAPTER needs semantics for, that B has published nothing about.
Listed so the gap is visible in the artifact a reviewer reads, instead of
being silently filled in by whatever the adapter happened to assume.
Each entry says what the adapter does in the absence of a published answer.
In every case the adapter's choice is the one that is safe to be wrong
about: it either refuses, or it reports the absence rather than assuming a
guarantee.

operation_id_format.adapter_behaviour: Treated as opaque. Required non-empty; never parsed for meaning. A format assumption would break on B's first real identifier.

expiry_semantics.adapter_behaviour: OperationBinding.expires_at is optional. When present it is enforced against the receiver's clock; when absent, `unbounded_authority` reports the absence instead of treating unbounded as safe. Inventing a default TTL would either expire real operations early or claim a bound the facade does not offer.

progress_state_vocabulary.adapter_behaviour: OperationState is this contract's own vocabulary, versioned under superplane_contracts v1, NOT a claim about B's wire values. A mapping layer belongs at the boundary when B publishes its states. UNKNOWN exists precisely so an unmappable value need not be rounded to a failure.

cancellation_surface.adapter_behaviour: Not modelled. The binding carries operation_id as the handle a cancellation would use, and nothing more. Modelling a cancel call against an unpublished surface would be the adapter inventing B's contract, which is the specific thing this note exists to prevent.

principal_resolution_mechanism.adapter_behaviour: The adapter requires a ResolvedPrincipal on the binding and refuses caller-supplied identity outright. HOW the facade resolves it is B's business and unobservable from here — which is a reason the live criterion stays open, not something a mock can settle.

accepted_progress_reports.$comment: A successful provision. The only shape whose `establishes_provisioned` is true.
In flight. Terminal is false; nothing may be concluded about the provider.
An outcome the facade could not determine. Terminal AND inconclusive — the case a consumer must not round to 'failed'. Carries a detail because the contract requires UNKNOWN to explain itself.
accepted_progress_reports.detail: provider API timed out after the operation was dispatched; outcome not established

rejected_variants.$comment: Not hypotheticals. Each shape below would compile, read plausibly in review, and silently weaken a guarantee the story names. They are why this file exists rather than prose alone.

rejected_variants.why_rejected: A report that does not name its operation could be about any concurrent one. With several provisions in flight, accepting it lets one operation's success be read as another's — the named-vs-positional failure the HITL contract also refuses.
The least actionable report the contract can carry, and the one most likely to be rounded to 'failed' by whoever reads it. Requiring a detail forces the facade to say what is unresolved.
A timestamp with no zone cannot be compared against a receiver's clock without guessing, and guessing produces an authorization that lapses hours early or late.

The tenant becomes a field the requester fills in. Refused even when the value matches the bound principal: a path that reads the caller's value is one comparison away from honouring a mismatched one, and comparisons get reordered, cached or made conditional. Design section 6, lines 398-407.

A read grant passed around as if it authorized provisioning. Refused at construction so it cannot travel, and re-checked by the adapter so the guarantee does not depend on validation staying in one place.

The two shapes the story forbids, together: an outcome read from an adapter-internal status field, and a provider's assertion about itself. Both are still true when the provider created nothing. Outcome comes from the facade's report or it is not outcome.

Not substitutable for B's contract, per repo-path-allocation.md. A direct read of a stored secret, an executor-minted long-lived credential, and the vault's credential-MANAGEMENT endpoints all lack the three properties that make the real thing safe: run binding, expiry, run-tied revocation. No field of this contract holds a credential, and the adapter module contains no secrets client.

what_this_fixture_does_not_establish: That B's operation facade behaves this way. It does not exist to behave any way — modules/harness/jobs/ is absent.
That provisioning works. Every facade and provider in the test suite is a mock, asserted to be a mock.

R14 acceptance 2 (live). Per acceptance-split.md rule 2, mock success closes no live criterion. Still gated on: a named account/environment, B's facade built, spend authorization, and a named cleanup owner.
R14 acceptance 1. That is the absence of the workflow_dispatch call and its foreign-repo PAT, owned by U17b, upstream, and untouched here.
